demo-integration.rationale: Talk passes its steps to the reusable Presentation. The shared Stage mounts the active Scene, while HowToScene builds its entities with scene-kit nodes. The inspected boundaries show no duplicated presentation navigation or scene host.
evidence: Talk renders Presentation with STEPS; Presentation delegates scene rendering to Stage.
HowToScene renders SceneLayer and the exported Box, Arrow, Label, Frame, SymbolChip, and Emphasis nodes.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine step records use the same Scene component and groupKey. Stage uses that key for the scene host across adjacent steps, so the Scene instance persists as its payload changes. Separately, HowToScene passes presentation-owned ENTITY and STEP_CARD_IDS values as node IDs; the node wrappers forward them to SceneNode, which assigns them to Motion layoutId.
evidence: Each of the nine STEPS entries names HowToScene, groupKey 'how-to-scene', and a distinct through value.
Stage keys a grouped scene host by groupKey and passes the active payload to the Scene.
HowToScene reuses entity constants and card IDs; SceneNode maps each ID to layoutId.

demo-integration.rationale: The public title supplied by Talk is consumed: Presentation passes it to Header, which renders it in browse mode. The demo's step payload drives HowToScene, its entity and card constants are used by scene nodes, and the shared canvas and layout constants used on this path reach Stage and useFitScale.
evidence: Talk supplies the title, Presentation forwards it, and Header renders the title in browse mode.
HowToScene reads payload.through and uses ENTITY and STEP_CARD_IDS in rendered nodes.
Presentation uses DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H; Stage uses LAYOUT_T and EASE; useFitScale reads STAGE_LAYOUT.

demo-integration.rationale: The progress and section controls expose aria-current alongside stable data-presentation-active attributes, and presentation-local CSS styles those active hooks. Footer implements the default 'made by and-scene' GitHub link in project source, with a stable attribution hook styled by the presentation-local CSS.
evidence: Footer sets aria-current='step' and data-presentation-active on the current progress button; Toc sets aria-current='location' and the same active hook on the current section.
Footer renders the default attribution link, and the demo stylesheet targets its attribution and active-state classes.

demo-integration.rationale: The registry only maps the demo route to Talk. Talk supplies presentation data and local styling to the shared Presentation boundary; the nine states, scene implementation, identities, and scene styling reside in the demo's own folder. The shared boundary handles hosting and chrome without demo-specific branching.
evidence: The registry lazily loads Talk for the demo slug.
Talk imports local steps and style; the local Scene and entity modules implement the demo diagram.
Presentation delegates rendering to the generic Stage and chrome components.

scene-kit.rationale: Each authored step has an identity, era, title, caption, and scene payload; the active step supplies both the scene and narration chrome.
evidence: STEPS defines distinct ids and narration with payloads; Presentation selects the active step, Stage renders its Scene and payload, and Header and Footer render its title and caption.

scene-kit.rationale: Displayed step numbers come from array positions.
evidence: Header formats index + 1 for the marker; Footer uses position + 1 for progress labels.

scene-kit.rationale: The generic Presentation boundary accepts the authored typed step array and forwards its payload to the scene without a cast.
evidence: Presentation<T> accepts PresentationProps<T>; Stage<T> passes step.payload; Talk passes STEPS typed as Step<HowToPayload>[] directly.

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing entities retain their identity and have an implemented layout projection path.
evidence: SceneNode renders a motion.div with layout and layoutId={id}; Stage supplies a LayoutGroup and retains the grouped scene host key.

scene-kit.rationale: New entities in the authored grouped scene mount directly, while the continuing entity layout path does not consume the entry delay's settlement value.
evidence: HowToScene conditionally mounts new Box and other nodes without Appear. Appear defines a delayed entry, but SceneNode's layout projection has no transition consuming LAYOUT_T and the sample does …

scene-kit.rationale: Ordinary authored entities that leave a grouped scene are removed conditionally without an entity presence boundary to retain them for exit animation.
evidence: HowToScene renders the ghost card only at step 5, so it is removed at step 6; Stage's AnimatePresence wraps the scene host, whose key remains the group key, rather than departing child entities.

scene-kit.rationale: Adjacent steps with the same group key and Scene component update one mounted scene instance.
evidence: Stage uses the shared group key as the host key and passes the changing payload into the same Scene; the focused test changes steps and asserts the scene mounted once.

scene-kit.rationale: Continuing children remain in the mounted grouped scene and are not wrapped in newcomer entry behavior.
evidence: Stage retains the grouped host; HowToScene keeps previously introduced entities rendered at subsequent payload values; SceneNode provides layout projection without Appear.

scene-kit.rationale: The grouped scene retains authored stacking and nesting through updates rather than reconstructing separate flattened scenes.
evidence: HowToScene keeps the conversation entities and tray together, accumulates cards, and nests the edited emphasis within its card; Stage keeps their shared scene instance mounted.

scene-kit.rationale: Present mode shows the active marker and title while omitting reading and step navigation chrome.
evidence: Header always renders the marker and renders only step.title in present mode; Presentation omits Toc and Footer omits caption, progress, and previous/next controls.

scene-kit.rationale: Browse mode provides the active title and caption, a wide-viewport table of contents, previous/next controls, and progress indicators.
evidence: Header renders step.title in browse mode; Footer renders the caption paragraph and controls; Presentation renders Toc, whose media rule hides it only below 820px.

scene-kit.rationale: Changing mode updates mode state without changing the active index.
evidence: usePresentationNav.toggleMode changes only mode; the focused test jumps to step two, switches mode, and asserts step two remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: The required forward and backward keys invoke bounded step navigation.
evidence: usePresentationNav handles ArrowRight, Space, and PageDown with next, and ArrowLeft and PageUp with prev.

scene-kit.rationale: The handler rejects predominantly vertical motion but does not reject multi-touch gestures.
evidence: usePresentationNav records x and y and compares their deltas, but both touch handlers use changedTouches[0] without checking touch count; no focused multi-touch rejection assertion is present.

scene-kit.rationale: Progress indicators jump to their indexed step, and table-of-contents entries jump to the first step of their era.
evidence: Footer calls goTo(position) for each progress button; Toc stores the first position for each era and calls goTo(position).

scene-kit.rationale: Active navigation controls expose semantic current state and a stable styling hook.
evidence: Footer progress buttons and Toc era buttons set aria-current and data-presentation-active according to the active index or era.

scene-kit.rationale: Presentation keyboard navigation yields when focus is on an interactive control.
evidence: isEditable detects buttons, links, inputs, selects, textareas, and editable elements; the key handler returns for those targets. The focused test sends ArrowLeft to the mode button and asserts the ac…

scene-kit.rationale: Backward navigation cannot set an index below zero.
evidence: goTo clamps to zero; the focused test sends ArrowLeft on the first step and asserts the first scene remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: Forward navigation cannot set an index beyond the last step.
evidence: goTo clamps to lastIndex; the focused test sends ArrowRight twice in a two-step presentation and asserts the second scene remains active.

scene-kit.rationale: The fit calculation uses one scale factor for both canvas axes and reserves space for mode-specific chrome.
evidence: useFitScale takes the minimum width and height ratio after subtracting per-mode reserves; Stage applies that same scale to the scene host and both frame dimensions.

scene-kit.rationale: The rendered stage defaults to the approved 880×380 authored canvas.
evidence: DESIGN_W and DESIGN_H are 880 and 380; Presentation uses them as default dimensions and passes them to Stage.

scene-kit.rationale: Primitives and chrome expose stable class and data attributes for author-owned styling.
evidence: SceneNode emits scene-kind and data-presentation-node hooks; Header, Footer, and Toc emit presentation classes and data hooks; the sample presentation CSS targets them.

scene-kit.rationale: Kit markup supplies layout geometry and motion but no fallback palette, font, border, shadow, card, or button treatment.
evidence: Presentation, Stage, chrome, and primitive inline styles contain positioning and sizing only; the visible palette and control treatments are supplied by presentation-owned CSS.

scene-kit.rationale: The kit renders through React and Motion with ordinary class and style hooks; its styling does not depend on a framework.
evidence: SceneNode accepts className and style directly, and the sample styles the kit through plain CSS; package dependencies contain no styling framework.

scene-kit.rationale: Authors can supply literal coordinates to kit nodes and use raw scene elements where needed.
evidence: SceneNode forwards style to its motion element; HowToScene supplies left, top, width, and height values to nodes and includes a positioned SVG arc.

scene-kit.rationale: The link exists, but its bottom-right placement comes only from presentation-owned CSS, so the kit does not provide the required default placement.
evidence: Footer renders the link without its own positioning style; the right and bottom offsets are defined by the sample presentation's .presentation-attribution rule.

scene-kit.rationale: The default attribution has stable CSS targets.
evidence: Footer renders presentation-attribution and data-presentation-attribution on the link; presentation CSS targets the class.

scene-kit.rationale: The header brand slot has no default brand and accepts explicitly supplied host content.
evidence: Presentation forwards renderHeaderBrand to Header; Header renders only that brand value in the slot. The focused default-render test asserts the slot is empty.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires one question at a time for missing topic, visual direction, and per-step content and visual intent.
evidence: Section 1 says to gather details only when missing, asks one question at a time, and lists the three detail groups.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs the agent to create from available information when the user chooses to proceed with incomplete details.
evidence: Section 1 requires restrained assumptions, disclosure of gaps, and no completeness gate after the user says to proceed.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill limits questions to missing details, so a prompt containing all requested details can proceed without redundant questions.
evidence: Section 1 says not to make the user repeat supplied details and to gather the listed details only when missing.

presentation-skill.rationale: A focused temporary-app test materializes the full bootstrap in a fresh target, checks required dependencies, installs them, builds, and verifies a registered presentation route in Chromium.
evidence: The test copies the bootstrap into a new temporary app, asserts every required dependency, runs npm install, lint, build, and verify, then asserts that the smoke scene renders without browser errors.

presentation-skill.rationale: The policy says to retain valid anchors, but no focused executable test or verified workflow evidence exercises an app with all three anchors and verifies that scaffolding is skipped.
evidence: The bootstrap test starts from a fresh target and copies the complete template; it does not construct an already scaffolded target.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused executable evidence constructs a target with only some anchors and verifies that missing anchors are added while existing anchors remain intact.
evidence: The bootstrap test copies the full template into a fresh target; it has no partial-anchor fixture or preservation assertions.

presentation-skill.rationale: The exercised bootstrap builds without Tailwind, and the test checks the copied scene kit for theme declarations; the scaffold CSS supplies only structural host and browser defaults.
evidence: The bootstrap test rejects Tailwind in the manifest, checks kit parity, scans kit source for visual theme defaults, and builds the materialized app.
The bootstrap index CSS contains browser and box-sizing rules, while its App.css supplies landing-page layout rules.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill instructs resolution from SKILL.md, but the executable test resolves the bootstrap from the test script's repository root. It does not verify bootstrap and presentation template lookup from the skill directory in an unrelated working directory.
evidence: The test derives root from its own import.meta.url and joins skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap; it never resolves a path from SKILL.md or exercises the presentation and step templates.

presentation-skill.rationale: No focused test or verified workflow constructs a monorepo and checks that the self-contained app lands under presentations/.
evidence: The bootstrap test creates one fresh app path and contains no workspace declaration, apps/ or packages/ fixture, or target-location assertion for a monorepo.

presentation-skill.rationale: The focused bootstrap test materializes a fresh non-monorepo app at the selected app root and installs, builds, and renders it there.
evidence: The test sets app to a new directory directly beneath its temporary workspace, copies the template to that directory, runs npm commands with app as cwd, and serves its registered route from that app.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires confirmation, but no focused test or verified workflow constructs an ambiguous nonempty target and verifies that writing waits for a user choice.
evidence: The bootstrap test begins with a fresh target and copies immediately; it has no nonempty target, simulated choice, or assertion that files remain untouched before confirmation.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires a presentation folder and registry entry, and the implemented registry and router make each registered slug load its presentation component.
evidence: Section 3 directs creation under src/presentations/<slug>/ and explicit registration.
The presentations array maps a slug to its Talk import; main.tsx finds that entry from the URL path and renders its lazy-loaded component.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill directs visual treatment into presentation or host CSS, and the delivered presentation imports its own stylesheet while the reusable kit supplies structural rendering.
evidence: Section 3 assigns color, type, spacing, borders, shadows, and component treatment to presentation or host CSS.
Talk imports local style.css, which defines the presentation and chrome treatment; the bootstrap test checks kit source for theme defaults.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly forbids replacing or unregistering existing presentations, and the registry and router support multiple entries without changing their route selection.
evidence: Section 3 requires one new explicit registry entry and says never to replace or unregister existing presentations.
The router selects an entry by slug from the presentations array.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires resolving an ambiguous modification target before changing files.
evidence: Section 1 instructs the agent to list registered presentations and ask which one to edit before changing files when the request does not identify a unique target.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill requires inspecting the selected presentation and steps, asking only about the requested change, and limiting edits to that presentation.
evidence: Sections 1 and 3 require preserving unrelated steps, files, and registry entries and making the smallest scoped changes without repeating the creation interview.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill makes build, browser render, navigation, and screenshot composition review prerequisites to a success report.
evidence: Section 4 requires npm run build, a real-browser target-route check, navigation exercise, and review of settled first, last, and key-step images; section 5 requires reporting those checks.

presentation-skill.rationale: The skill explicitly requires fixing failures and rerunning checks before claiming success.
evidence: Section 4 says to fix build failures, not claim success after a required check fails, and rerun build, render, and inspection after fixes; section 5 requires plainly reporting an unresolved failure.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifier rejects a missing canonical route or step and exits nonzero. The missing-sample fixture removes the route and asserts failure output.
evidence: scripts/verify.mjs checks the canonical registry entry and ordered steps, then sets process.exitCode to 1 on error.
The missing sample case in scripts/test-verification.mjs removes the registry entry and requires a nonzero status and “Sample check failed” output.

verification-tooling.rationale: Both delivered verifiers bind Vite to 127.0.0.1 and use that address for readiness probes and browser navigation.
evidence: The root verifier builds origin from 127.0.0.1 and uses it for fetch and page.goto.
The bootstrap verifier uses the same address for preview binding, fetch, and page.goto.

verification-tooling.rationale: Each verifier checks the child before fetching, but accepts any successful response at the fixed port without checking that the spawned child served it or remained alive afterward. A stale server can satisfy readiness while the new child exits.
evidence: Both readiness loops break immediately on a successful fetch; neither checks the child after that response or ties the response to the child process.

verification-tooling.rationale: The verifiers collect console and page errors, and a focused fixture asserts a runtime browser error at step 3. No focused executable case injects and asserts a console error, so the required evidence for both error channels is incomplete.
evidence: Both verifiers register pageerror and console-error listeners and include step numbers in failure messages.
The runtime browser error fixture throws during step 3; scripts/test-verification.mjs has no console-error injection case.

verification-tooling.rationale: A focused fixture disables next navigation; the verifier detects that the step index did not advance and reports step 2 with a nonzero outcome.
evidence: The stalled transition case replaces next with a no-op and asserts nonzero status plus the step-2 failure message.
Both verifiers wait for the expected data-step-index and throw a step-numbered transition error when it fails to advance.

verification-tooling.rationale: The project exposes a separate inspect command that launches a preview, opens the requested presentation in Playwright, and writes screenshots locally. The bootstrap provides the same command and helper.
evidence: The inspect script in each package invokes its project-local helper.
Each helper opens the requested slug and writes PNG files under inspection/.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper captures each indexed step from the requested preview route and waits for the next rendered step index before continuing. The executable inspection fixture asserts two screenshots for its two steps and nine for the reference presentation.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs navigates to the slug URL, loops over data-step-count, saves an indexed PNG, and advances via ArrowRight with a data-step-index wait.
scripts/test-inspection.mjs registers a two-step fixture, asserts two PNGs, then asserts nine PNGs for the reference route.

verification-tooling.rationale: Capture waits a fixed 900 ms. It neither observes animation completion nor consumes a transition contract shared with persistent scene motion; the test only checks elapsed time.
evidence: Both helpers call waitForTimeout(900) before screenshots.
Stage consumes LAYOUT_T for its host transition, while SceneNode uses layout animation without a shared capture contract. The inspection test asserts only a minimum total duration.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper measures visible text and chrome rectangles and reports collisions. A focused browser fixture creates unmarked node overlap and a header collision, then asserts warning output for both.
evidence: The candidate selection includes scene nodes and nested header text; intersecting rectangles produce a visible text/chrome overlap warning.
The inspection fixture creates unmarked colliding boxes and a header collision, then asserts the overlap warning and the header collision text.

verification-tooling.rationale: The overlap scan excludes elements inside an explicit allow-overlap marker. A focused fixture places a marked box over another box, confirms that pair is absent from warnings, and still requires unrelated collisions to be reported.
evidence: Candidate filtering excludes elements with a data-presentation-allow-overlap ancestor.
The inspection fixture asserts that the marked pair is not reported while requiring the unmarked overlap warning.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper compares computed styles of rendered active and inactive navigation controls. A focused fixture makes those styles equal and asserts the indistinct-state warning.
evidence: The helper compares color, backgroundColor, borderColor, opacity, and transform on active and inactive elements.
The fixture CSS equalizes those properties and the test requires “visually indistinct” in the helper output.

verification-tooling.rationale: The helper inspects rendered attribution visibility and computed style. A focused fixture restores browser-default anchor styling and asserts the resulting warning.
evidence: The helper reports missing or hidden attribution, browser-default link styling, and undersized text.
The fixture applies all: revert to attribution and requires “browser-default” in the helper output.

It disclosed that the presentation skill’s creation, modification, and repair journeys were unexercised. Together with the limited navigation and scene interaction evidence, these omissions leave a substantial share of the specified user-visible behavior uncovered.

candidate-ea0a60dbd194e9b3 declares diff base 7998a2f65c006c2a56f57b1801aa1ab143516448 and plans checks for viewport validation and phone attribution.
candidate-8b05052c24bc060d records the zero-dimension CLI result and short-phone attribution inspection at the final revision.

testing-evidence.rationale: The handoff reports NOT READY and discloses the unexercised interaction flows, environment limit, absent CI and automated suite evidence, remaining mobile legibility question, and visual warning results without claiming full acceptance.
evidence: candidate-8ffe029c8fbbadf8 states acceptance did not converge and gives NOT READY as the tester status.
candidate-1f0a8ba6e3c22a13 discloses I-001, U3, absent build/test CI evidence, and the short-phone inspector’s lack of advisory warnings.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate surfaced the consequential mobile legibility issue, the unexercised skill flows, and other unresolved behavior questions.
evidence: The assumptions ledger records U3: fixed-canvas scene labels become only a few screen pixels tall at 390×844.
The ledger records U4/I-001: AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 remain unexercised.

evidence: The ledger says the approved AT-003 plan expects a narrow-viewport pass and that round-0 F-001 was recorded because the plan requires readable content.
The browser evidence describes narrow labels as difficult to read, and the round-2 log says they remain proportionally tiny.

assumption-handling.rationale: The candidate deferred reproduced unreadable mobile labels to a product decision and reported no current defect, despite the stated readability requirement. That disposition understates the action needed to meet acceptance.
evidence: U3 asks whether small proportional scaling is acceptable for release, while acknowledging that AT-003 expects a narrow-viewport pass.
The tester handoff says 'No current product defect was found' and recommends reviewing U3 as a mobile readability tradeoff.

assumption-handling.rationale: The handoff preserves the unresolved mobile legibility decision, the missing interaction-flow coverage, the acceptance status, and actionable next steps. Its misclassification of legibility is scored separately.
evidence: The tester handoff states that phone-size label legibility remains U3 for a human product/design decision.
It identifies AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004 as unexercised, marks acceptance NOT READY, and proposes an independent skill invocation path or an explicit decision to leave those flows untested.
